Local cerebral metabolic rate for glucose in frontal cortex, as printed on the ordinate.
Note: SECONDARY: these are the frontal-cortex lCMRGlc values of Chugani et al. (1987) replotted, not a new measurement; N = 29, as this paper's Table 2 prints, matching the 29 patients of Chugani's Table 1. Digitisation: the open circles were pixel-digitised from the embedded page bitmap (1890 x 2850 px, 8-bit grey, PDF p. 4) by Feinberg_etal_1990_Figure1_extract.py (conda env 'python'; pymupdf, numpy, scipy), run 2026-10-31; a second run reports 'snapshot unchanged'. Both axes are SINGLE LINEAR axes; the abscissa is calibrated on the eight printed 5-year ticks and the ordinate on the row centres of the printed tick labels (the ordinate rule is slightly skewed on this scan, so a fixed-column tick scan misses some). Circles are found two ways and merged: the white region each ring encloses, and normalised cross-correlation against a ring template cut from an isolated circle, which recovers rings the fitted gamma curve has broken; marker_detection records which found each point. ESTIMATED ERROR +/- 0.5 umol/min/100 g and +/- 0.2 y. POINTS CONTAINED vs RESOLVED: the panel contains 29 plotted points and 28 were individually resolved; the 29th could not be separated from its neighbour in the 3-8 year cluster and is ABSENT, not inferred. CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE (built here as Chugani_etal_1987_Table2 and Chugani_etal_1987_Figure2A): assigning the resolved points to Chugani's four printed age bins by age rank (bin membership is fixed by the patients' printed ages, n = 7/4/12/6, with the one missing point taken from the 3-8 y bin), the bin means reproduce Chugani's Table 2 frontal-cortex means to +0.85, +0.24, +0.05 and +0.77 umol/min/100 g - all within 1.0. The plotted range, 15.1 to 60.3, matches the 14.8 to 59.7 range of the frontal-cortex points digitised from Chugani's Fig. 2A. A point-by-point comparison is NOT possible: neither figure resolves all 29 points (28 here, 25 there) and there is no key to pair them on.
